faq.question: How much does window replacement cost in Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Palo Alto homeowners typically invest $10,000 to $25,000 for a full window replacement project. This world-famous Silicon Valley city — with median home values exceeding $3 million — features original Eichler flats, Craftsman homes near University Avenue, and custom estate homes in Crescent Park and Old Palo Alto. Large Eichler floor-to-ceiling glass systems require specialized installation. Single window installation starts at approximately $750.

faq.question: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Yes. Palo Alto requires a building permit for window replacements. Eichler homes and properties in Old Palo Alto's historic residential areas may require additional design review to ensure replacement windows respect the architectural character of the home. Our team manages all Palo Alto permit applications on your behalf.

faq.question: Is it worth replacing 20-year-old windows in Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Often yes. Twenty-year-old windows in Palo Alto commonly show fogged glass, drafts and weak locks. Newer ENERGY STAR units improve comfort and curb appeal; Deluxe Windows compares payback against your utility rates and home style before recommending replacement.

faq.question: Should I choose fiberglass or vinyl windows in Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Vinyl is the value pick for most Palo Alto replacements and handles Bay Area weather well. Fiberglass (including Marvin Ultrex) is stronger, more stable in temperature swings and better for larger openings or coastal exposure. We show both side by side in the showroom and on-site.

faq.question: How long does window replacement take in Palo Alto?
faq.answer: Most Palo Alto projects are measured in one visit and installed in one to three working days once products arrive — typically four to eight weeks after ordering, depending on brand and custom sizes.
